nodes.title: Spoken Devanagari fractions earn evidence (4A, main's 14.4 item from 4B's finding). classify() over the 52 fraction-key kit items x 4 Devanagari spoken forms of the key ('<n> बटा <d>', '<n> बता <d>', '+ होगा', 'मेरे ख्याल से +'): correct 0/208 before, 208/208 after (156 by the code number path). Wrong forms (n/(d+1), (n+1)/d, d/n, and 'मुझे बता दो' on every item): 0/208 credited before and after; 'मुझे बता दो' no evidence 52/52. Three changes: spoken-number.js reads बटा / बता as OVER (बता only between two numbers) and a Devanagari दो after a verb stem as the verb unless a fraction claims it; learner/affect.js no longer reads '<n> बता दो' as asking for the answer; tailAgrees reads a spoken Devanagari fraction as the number itself. Side-effect check (main): tailAgrees and unitsAfterNumbers old vs new over 2,008 Devanagari sim-lab child lines x their item keys: only the 2 fraction lines moved; 0 unit readings moved. A first version that kept vowel signs in wordToks moved 206 (then 832) other Devanagari tail verdicts and was replaced. Shared fixture: 4B's tests/fixtures/spoken-fractions.json (34 cases, the engine's valuesOf and duplex/understand.js valuesIn test the same file): the grader read 32/34 at first ('2 बता दो' lost the digit numerator; 'एक बार और दिखा दो' read 1) and 34/34 after two narrow rules: a digit numerator stays open before an OVER word with a number after it (and a digit denominator then closes the fraction), and 'एक बार' with words after it is 'once', not 1. The grader keeps 'एक' in running Hindi as 1 ('मेरे ख्याल से एक'), where 4B's readers count it only alone or in 'एक बटा'. Old vs new numberPhrases / spokenNumber / unitsAfterNumbers / statedResults / selfCorrected over 3,162 sim-lab child lines (636 Devanagari): 25 lines moved, 21 'ek baar / एक बार' narrative lines (once) and 4 '<digit> over <digit>' lines now read as one value ('2 over 5' -> 0.4, '1.5 over 9' -> 1/6); 0 unit readings moved. The 208/208 and 0/208 still hold.

No affirmation that approves what nobody said (open-r143-affirm-on-no-answer; brain/say.js affirmOpenerFix on every lane's final reply, never a safeguard). (a) not_yet / partial verdict or truly empty input: the leading affirmation goes; (b) a right answer that opens No / nahi / नहीं: a bare Yes / Haan / हाँ opener becomes Right / Sahi / सही. Same function over the sim lab's transcripts: 14.2 decided Director 860 turns 1 stripped, 0 left; e46a281 decided 1,698 turns 3 polarity rewrites, 0 left; f444f064 continuer OOS 415 turns 0 (a 'Right-align' opener is not an affirmation); p30 re-run 1 polarity rewrite ('Yes, Pihu—earthworm has no legs' -> 'Right, Pihu—…'). Not covered: the polarity case on the agent lane's streamed first clause.

Keeping Devanagari vowel signs (\p{M}) in spoken-number.js wordToks so 'बटा' tokenises whole (4A, 14.4 spoken fractions): it moved 206 of 2,008 sim-lab Devanagari tail verdicts that had nothing to do with fractions, e.g. 'पाँच मीटर' for '5 m' true -> false. Replaced by reading a spoken Devanagari fraction as one number before tokenising (DEVA_FRACTION), which moved only the 2 fraction lines.

Fixing the keep-marks side effect by having tailAgrees ignore a Devanagari tail entirely (4A, 14.4 spoken fractions): it moved 832 of 2,008 sim-lab Devanagari tail verdicts the other way (contradicting tails stopped vetoing). Replaced by DEVA_FRACTION with wordToks unchanged (2 moved, both fraction lines false -> true, 0 unit readings moved).

The deep-kind audit's 1,927 marks are measured before they are applied: TAXILA_KIT_DEEP_MARKS=1 (off by default) loads data/kits/deep-marks-2026-10-15.json as deep: false through the kit loader; the patch itself (main's deep-kind-fix, items.js plainEvidence) is applied on claude/r4-conversation and changes nothing while no kit carries deep: false. The sim lab's 2x2 (marks off/on x a kind-only / audit-aware decided child) decides. Reversal: on apply, write the marks into the kits (evals/kit-deep-kinds/apply.mjs --write) and remove the switch and the list; on reject, remove both and keep the patch's code inert.
